review.reason:
The geometry is strategically credible and the artwork maps confidently to the connected routing, but the putting-green treatment needs regeneration before publication.

Hole 1 is the 300-yard par 4 from T1 along the lower shoreline to G1 near T2. The artwork retains its substantial left-side lake, right fairway bunker and two small left/back greenside bunkers. The narrow landing strip provides a controlled placement alternative to attacking the green directly. Its 20 simulated safe tee options warrant caution, but the preview shows a usable corridor rather than an obligatory water carry.

Hole 2 is the 229-yard par 3 from T2 toward the large G2 near T3. Its right-side lake, left approach bunker and three left/back greenside bunkers remain recognizable. The relatively generous target supports center-green play, while the long approach demands distance control. Lake extent and target proportions are sufficiently faithful.

Hole 3 is the dry 584-yard par 5 returning from T3 through the long bending fairway to G3. The broad staged route contrasts with a more aggressive line challenging the inside trees. The illustration preserves the large approach bunker and small greenside groups on both sides. Its 62 safe tee options support, without proving, fair playability.

The short shoreline par 4, long wet par 3 and dry bending par 5 provide excellent within-round contrast. Punchbowl greens recur frequently in recent rounds, but the longer version here and the dry dogleg finish provide sufficient differentiation.

The artwork preserves the compact 5:3 shared property, folded routing, green-to-next-tee connections, continuous interior grass and selective groves. However, especially around G3 and G1, the putting surfaces have outlined edges and multiple concentric turf bands forming broad ringed surrounds. This does not meet the required single natural putting surface with only a narrow, low-contrast fringe. Regenerate those surrounds without changing the mapped green footprints, flags, hazards or routing. No geometry edits are justified.
